correctness.rationale: The corrected RESULT.md retains the equality theorem and closes a gap in the cited majorant argument. In Allu–Kumar's Eq. (2.6), the constant Schur group's g² coefficient is p²(4−p²)(172−49p²), negative for 172/49<p²<4; a termwise triangle bound cannot retain that sign. The upper bound itself survives: grouping the constant, linear and quadratic terms in −g gives A+Bexp(iψ)−Cexp(2iψ), where C/B≤2/17 and C/A≤4/27 in this regime, hence B(A−C)>4AC. Subtracting the absolute square from (A+B−C)² gives the nonnegative factorization in repaired Step 2. All other groups have valid separate absolute bounds. Consequently exactly the same Bernstein certificate proves strictness for p<2 and |g|<1. Independently reconstructed inverse coefficients by Lagrange inversion and Schur recursion; reconstructed the source majorant's Phi (Bernstein minima 0 and 160 in the first p-slice) and the reduced unimodular defect by exact Chebyshev substitution (Bernstein minima 78336, 78848 on the half-boxes). Thus equality forces p=2, or |g|=1 and either p=0 or g=−1. For the boundary cases the Schur transform terminates: p=2 gives Koebe, g=−1 gives z/(1−pz+z²), and p=0 gives z/(1−gz²). Rotations recover precisely the two-pole family. Substitution in w(1−az+bz²)=z gives the stated inverse coefficients and determinant b³; its starlikeness follows by averaging the two positive-real-part Cayley kernels.
residual_risks: The frozen proof used the majorant as a premise without addressing the negative quadratic coefficient; its validity is established here by an analytical phase estimate, not by trying sample coefficients.
